rationale: The Living Motion sensor (SEN-M1) was running firmware 1.1 speaking the legacy v2 protocol, which the HB-200 base station (fw 4.5) no longer supports, producing E-305 "protocol v2 not supported" and a connected_no_events status. The standard L1 fix — replacing the battery to exceed 30% and triggering the OTA upgrade to 1.4 (v3) — completed successfully and the sensor resumed sending alerts, confirming the root cause and resolution.

repair_steps: Confirm the Living Motion sensor (SEN-M1) firmware is now 1.4 and protocol v3.
Verify the sensor status is 'online' and events are being received.
Ask the customer to test the sensor by triggering motion and checking for alerts.
If all checks pass, close the ticket as resolved.

args.query: E-305 peripheral firmware outdated OTA upgrade protocol v2 to v3

results.text: The peripheral firmware speaks a radio protocol the base station no longer supports, or vice versa. Frontline action: trigger OTA upgrade of the peripheral. If OTA is not available for the device or fails twice, escalate to FAE as protocol conflict.

Peripheral firmware is upgraded over the air (OTA) from the base station. Requirements: device within normal signal range, battery above 30 percent. CAM-S1 1.x upgrades to 2.1 (protocol v3). SEN-D1 1.0 upgrades to 1.3, SEN-M1 1.1 upgrades to 1.4. CAM-I2 hardware revision A with firmware 1.2 cannot be upgraded to protocol v3.

Base station firmware updates are pushed automatically at night. HB-200 firmware 4.5 removes support for the legacy v2 radio protocol. Peripherals still running v2 firmware must be upgraded to v3 firmware before or after the base station update, otherwise they disconnect.

It avoids unsupported claims: the customer reported the firmware update completed and alerts resumed, so stating the sensor is updated and working is supported.
